answer: A tundra vine guards an agent economy with echo-grafted cuttings: every new identity must graft one cutting onto the communal vine, and the graft is sealed by a chain of sequential echoes from distinct established agents, growing one ring at a time, so the first fake needs 1 echo, the second 7, the third 19, the tenth 271 and the twentieth 1,141, and twenty fakes together need 8,000 echoes. Bulk farming fails because each echo must be heard before the next is sounded, so no echo can be rushed, copied, or bought in parallel, like a message passed from voice to voice across a frozen plain.
